title: Alternating, Ratio & Root Tests
summary: The alternating series test handles sign-flipping series; absolute convergence is stronger than conditional. The ratio and root tests examine the growth of $|a_n|$ and settle most series with factorials or exponentials.

absolute convergence.in_class: Implies the series itself converges — the strong kind.

root test.in_class: Same thresholds as the ratio test; good for $n$-th powers.

error bound.plain: Alternating series error is under the next term.

factorial growth.in_class: Ratio test shines when factorials appear.

concept_sections.heading: The alternating series test
concept_sections.explanation: If a series alternates sign and its magnitudes $b_n$ decrease to $0$, it converges. The error after $N$ terms is at most the first omitted term $b_{N+1}$.

concept_sections.heading: Absolute vs conditional
concept_sections.explanation: If $\sum|a_n|$ converges, the series converges absolutely (and unconditionally). If the series converges but $\sum|a_n|$ diverges, it's conditional — order-sensitive.
math_steps: If not, but the series still converges ⇒ conditional.

concept_sections.heading: The ratio test
concept_sections.explanation: Compute $L=\lim\left|\dfrac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|$. If $L<1$ it converges absolutely; $L>1$ (or $\infty$) diverges; $L=1$ is inconclusive. Ideal for factorials and exponentials.
math_steps: Form the ratio of consecutive terms.

concept_sections.heading: The root test
concept_sections.explanation: Compute $L=\lim\sqrt[n]{|a_n|}$ with the same thresholds. Use it when $a_n$ has an $n$-th power, like $\left(\tfrac{n}{n+1}\right)^{n^2}$.

concept_sections.heading: Choosing a test
concept_sections.explanation: Factorials or products ⇒ ratio test; $n$-th powers ⇒ root test; simple sign flips ⇒ alternating test; otherwise comparison or integral. A quick scan picks the tool.
math_steps: Match to the most efficient test.
